analysis: The code snippet calls Integer.parseInt(parts[1]) after splitting a masterUrl that matches the regex ".*:\\d*". This regex allows zero or more digits after the colon. If parts[1] is empty (e.g., masterUrl ends with colon) or contains a numeric string that exceeds the range of int (overflow), parseInt will throw NumberFormatException. The code does not validate parts[1] before parsing, so the exception is not avoided.
remark: The NumberFormatException can be triggered when parts[1] is empty (e.g., masterUrl like "host:") because the regex allows zero digits, or when the port number is too large to fit in an int (e.g., "999999999999") as parseInt throws for overflow.
